name: Kirkstall Abbey ginkgo

location.address: Outside the Abbot's Lodging, Kirkstall Abbey, Abbey Road, Leeds LS5 3EH

access: Ruins and grounds of Kirkstall Abbey, run by Leeds Museums and Galleries, set in a public park on the north bank of the River Aire; opening hours and any admission are on the Leeds Museums page (general admission tickets bookable on site), which has not been settled to a price here. Say 'check opening times' on the page.
verify_notes: Tree stands outside the Abbot's Lodging in the abbey grounds. Age: Yorkshire Evening Post (17 Nov 2026) says it is believed to date from around the late 19th century, when parts of the site were landscaped; the interpretation board transcribed on HMDB marker 278660 says it 'was only planted in the late 19th century' (the board is probably the YEP's source, so these two are not independent on the date). Wording to keep: the tree is NOT medieval despite the setting; a 2017 blog claims the abbot's garden had a ginkgo, not supported by the board. Colonel John North bought the abbey buildings in the late 1800s and gave the ruins and grounds to Leeds Corporation (YEP); no source ties his gift to this planting, do not bridge. Board: many people think the tree has medicinal properties (popular belief). Draws local press each November when it turns bright gold: YEP photo piece 17 Nov 2026 and West Leeds Dispatch 16 Nov 2025, plus a Flickr photo dated 20 Nov 2024 (nigel_turner) show it alive and gold. ALIVE: yes, YEP 17 Nov 2026. PIN: HMDB marker for the Abbot's Lodging board at 53 49.215 N, 1 36.382 W (53.82026,-1.60636), the board mentions the tree 'outside the abbot's lodging'; no tree-level coordinate found (Flickr not geotagged), so approximate on a 30 m site. No girth or height in any source. Season: strong autumn gold, mid to late November per the press pieces (best_time candidate for the writer's phenology check).

name: Bingley Arms yew

location.address: The Bingley Arms, Church Lane, Bardsey, Leeds LS17 9DR

access: Customers' beer garden of a public house open to the public (pub opening hours); no entry fee, the tree is seen from the garden.

location_site.name: Beer garden of the Bingley Arms, Bardsey

verify_notes: THIN, flagged. Wikipedia: the beer garden is home to a yew tree that pre-dates the Bingley Arms. Yorkshire Post (1 Jul 2019): 'in the beer garden stands a yew tree even older than the pub itself'. e2e.bike (undated page): 'something reckoned to be over a thousand years old, looking pretty youthful'. The over-a-thousand-years figure is a pub-lore estimate, not measured: no girth, no register entry, no Ancient Yew Group record found, and the pub's own age claim (905 to 953) has no historic study behind it (Wikipedia), the stone building is 18th century. Age range here is deliberately broad: age_min 300 is only because the yew pre-dates an 18th-century building; the writer must say 'said to be' and give no sharper number. Wording note: the e2e line says the tree looks 'pretty youthful', i.e. not a hollow giant. ALIVE: thin, latest source naming it is the 2019 Yorkshire Post piece; lifecheck RECENT 2023 for the pub only, not the tree. PIN: OSM pub node 4935984922 at 53.8815587,-1.4482891; the tree's position inside the garden is not known, so approximate on a 30 m site. Bardsey is in the City of Leeds district, about 7 miles NNE of the centre. Ask the reader for girth. A photograph or a reader's GPS would upgrade it.
